exposure: Pregnancy complicated by fetal growth restriction and gestational hypertension
outcome: Successful maternal management of APS and endocarditis through cardiac surgery during pregnancy
Newborn survival and good health at follow-up
cohort: A 38-year-old pregnant woman at 15 weeks gestation with primary antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) complicated by Libman-Sacks tricuspid valve endocarditis.
finding: Multidisciplinary management involving anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy and cardiac surgery during pregnancy successfully managed a rare case of Libman-Sacks tricuspid valve endocarditis in a pregnant woman with primary antiphospholipid syndrome, resulting in the birth of a healthy newborn.
mod_finding: An emergency cesarean section was performed at 35 weeks gestation due to fetal distress, specifically repeated decelerations and abnormal short-term variability on c-CTG, in a pregnancy complicated by fetal growth restriction and gestational hypertension.
followup_time: At least 2 months post-birth (neonatal discharge), with an unspecified longer-term update on current health.
